title: Settings is a System
summary: This reel teaches how to design a robust settings system by categorizing actions based on their impact. It covers the use of instant vs. explicit save models, task-based grouping, search functionality, and high-friction 'danger zones' for destructive actions.

transcript.text: Most of it is harmless.
The bottom deletes everything.
Settings is a system.
Instant. Or explicit.
Toggles apply instantly. Flip, done.
Identity fields don't.
They get a save bar and a cancel.
Match the model to the blast radius.
Forty settings and one list reads like a phone book.
Group by task.
Hide advanced behind one click.
Stripe splits by job: payments, billing, team.
Power users never scroll. They search.
One input finds any setting buried three levels deep.
Highlight the match, show the path.
Every changed setting shows a dot and a reset.
VS Code marks every override with a colored bar.
Users experiment when undo is one click away.
Destructive actions live in quarantine.
Red border, bottom of the page.
Deleting means typing the name first.
The button stays dead until the name matches.
Settings is a system. Follow for more UI engineering. Save this for your next project.

on_screen_text: instant for preferences • explicit for identity
group by task, not by table
type to filter • enter to jump
design_principles: Match the save model to the blast radius (low stakes = instant, high stakes = explicit)
Group settings by task or user intent rather than database tables
Provide search for large settings lists to support power users
Visually indicate modified states to encourage experimentation and easy undoing
Increase friction for destructive actions using quarantine zones and confirmation typing
before_after: Transforms a flat, unorganized list of 40 settings into a structured, searchable system with clear visual feedback and safety measures for destructive actions.
